open_points.subject: resume of service_unreachable elements after grant revocation
open_points.text: State 0 action: "resume a run ... the nodes waiting on an unreachable service are tried again, whatever else the run waits for." vs A14 rule 2: "an element whose grant was revoked meanwhile waits for approval instead."
open_points.question: On resume, must every `service_unreachable` element always perform a resend attempt, or may authority re-check convert some of them to `owner_approval` without resending?
options: Always attempt resend for every `service_unreachable` element named by resume.
Re-check authority first; if no valid authority, do not resend and switch that element to `owner_approval`.
open_points.default_guess: Re-check authority first and switch to `owner_approval` when grant/approval no longer authorizes send.

open_points.subject: approval digest mismatch when a standing grant exists
open_points.text: Owner decision 18 (State 0): "Any difference at send ... asks again." vs M24/A10: "An approved, unused approval whose `request_digest` no longer matches ... the kernel then sends under an active grant when one applies, otherwise requests a new approval."
open_points.question: If a previously approved request no longer matches at send time and a standing grant is active, does the kernel have to ask again, or may it send under the grant?
options: Always ask again on any approval/request mismatch, regardless of grant.
Treat mismatched approval as unusable but allow send under active grant.
open_points.default_guess: Allow send under active grant; ask again only when no grant applies.

open_points.subject: size ceiling semantics for `many` value inputs/cases
open_points.text: A12 rule 1: "each value ... is within `stored_value_bytes_max`; for a `many` port, is a JSON array whose every element fits it." A04 rule 1 similarly checks fit/size but does not define whether size is per whole array or per element.
open_points.question: For a `many` `value` port, is `stored_value_bytes_max` enforced on the whole array value, on each element, or both?
options: Both whole array and each element.
open_points.default_guess: Enforce on the whole array value (with element schema validation separately).

open_points.subject: transport cutoff between `not_sent` and `unknown`
open_points.text: A09 rule 5: "'Nothing could be sent' holds only when the failure happened before the kernel wrote the first byte of the request; any failure after that ... is 'may have been sent'."
open_points.question: What exact transport event is authoritative for 'first byte written' when the HTTP client buffers, retries socket writes internally, or uses TLS framing?
options: Use application-level 'request write started' callback/flag from client library.
Use successful kernel-level socket write of any request bytes.
Use TLS-record write boundary after handshake completion.
open_points.default_guess: Classify by the earliest client-library event that confirms any request bytes were handed to the transport (then treat failures as `unknown`).
